verdict: CLAUDE wins on a common scoring basis at 72.96 xPts, +6.66 over YOUR current team (66.30) and +6.34 over Gemini normalised (66.62). Your team does NOT already match the best plan — it needs a move. The engines agree on everything that is normally contentious (captain B.Fernandes, vice Gabriel, no chip, nine of eleven XI slots) which is why conviction is HIGH: this is not a week where the models are pulling in opposite directions on strategy. The entire gap is one operational fact — Frimpong is confirmed injured and your cache says AVAILABLE. YOU are currently starting a player who will score 0. Gemini catches half the problem (it benches him) but then rolls the transfer and, forced to fill the slot, starts Awoniyi (xPts 0.32, FDR 5 away, not in his club's predicted XI) over E.Le Fée (5.28, nailed, FDR 2) — a direct Consistency Rule (A) violation worth ~4.96 xPts. Claude fixes the whole problem: spends the free transfer, upgrades the dead slot into an XI starter (N.Williams 6.66), banks 0.5m and restores bench autosub cover. FLAGGED DISAGREEMENTS: (1) transfer — roll vs spend, Claude is right because medical-bay is a confirmed source, not a projection; (2) Awoniyi vs E.Le Fée — YOU and Claude agree, Gemini is the outlier and should be overruled; (3) Hume — genuine coin flip, ~1.4 xPts, safe to ignore either way. Gemini's self-reported 49.44 should not be compared directly to 72.96; its method under-counts. The honest engine gap is 6.34, not 23.5. Accept it this week, do not compound it by moving the armband, and make funding him the GW2/GW3 priority.
